A1: Start with: The best thing today was…
Use the past: I went / I ate / I saw…
Add how you felt: It was great / fun / relaxing.
Start with: I'm good / tired / happy today.
Then say why: …because I…
Useful words: busy, sleepy, excited, stressed.
Start with: Today I ate… / For breakfast I had…
Use 'had' for meals: I had rice and beans.
Add: It was delicious / OK / too much.
Start with: Today it's sunny / rainy / cloudy / hot / cold.
Add: I like / don't like this weather because…
Useful: It's windy. It's a little cold.
Start with: I woke up at… (seven o'clock).
Add: Then I… (took a shower / had breakfast).
Useful: early, late, on time.
Start with: After class, I'm going to…
Examples: have dinner, watch TV, go to bed.
Add when: at eight o'clock / tonight.
Start with: Yesterday I…
Past verbs: went, worked, watched, cooked, visited.
Add with who or where: with my family / at home.
Start with: This weekend I'm going to…
Ideas: go to the beach, visit my parents, rest.
Add: I'm excited / I need to rest.
Start with: My day was good / busy / tiring.
Then say one thing: I had a meeting / I worked a lot.
Useful: boring, interesting, stressful.
Start with: These days I'm listening to…
Add the type: pop, rock, samba, podcasts.
Add: I like it because…
A2: Start with: The best thing this week was when I…
Use the simple past: went, met, finished, got.
Add a feeling: I was really happy / relieved.
Start with: Last weekend I…
Use time words: On Saturday… On Sunday… Then…
Add: It was relaxing / a lot of fun.
Start with: Tonight I'm going to…
Or a plan: I'm meeting / I'm having dinner with…
Add: I'm looking forward to it.
Start with: Something new in my life is…
Use: I've just started… / I recently bought…
Explain: It's important because…
Start with: The last thing that made me laugh was…
Describe: My friend told me… / I saw a video…
Add: It was so funny because…
Start with: At the moment I'm reading / watching…
Describe it: It's about… The main character is…
Give your opinion: I really like it / It's OK.
Start with: I slept well / badly last night.
Explain: because it was hot / I went to bed late.
Useful: I woke up a few times. I feel rested.
Start with: For lunch I had…
Add where: at home / at a restaurant near work.
Add opinion: It was delicious / too heavy.
Start with: I'm looking forward to…
Remember: looking forward to + -ing / noun.
Explain when and why.
Start with: This week at work…
Use: We had… / My boss said… / I finished…
Add: It was good news / a bit stressful.
B1: Start with: Since our last class, the best thing was…
Use present perfect for recent news: I've just… / I've finally…
Add details: who, where, how you felt.
Start with: Lately I've been thinking about…
Explain the situation and why it matters.
Useful: I'm not sure if… / I'm trying to decide…
Start with: Recently I learned that…
Say where: I read it / I watched a video / someone told me.
Add: It surprised me because…
Start with: Something that annoyed me was…
Describe what happened, then how you reacted.
Useful: It drives me crazy when… / I couldn't believe…
Start with: If I had a free day, I would…
Use 'would' for each idea: I would sleep in, I would…
Add why: …because I haven't had time to…
Start with: I recently had an interesting conversation with…
Report it: She told me that… / He asked me if…
Add: What I found interesting was…
Start with: To relax this weekend, I…
Give two activities and how they helped.
Useful: I needed a break / It helped me disconnect.
Start with: I need to decide whether to… or…
Give pros and cons: On the one hand… on the other hand…
Finish: I'm leaning towards…
Start with: A piece of news that caught my attention was…
Summarize it in two sentences.
Give your opinion: I think… because…
Start with: So far, my week has been…
Use present perfect: I've had… / I've been working on…
Add what's still coming: and tomorrow I'm going to…
B2: Start with: Since we last spoke, the highlight has been…
Add context and why it mattered to you.
Useful: What made it special was…
Start with: I used to think… but now I believe…
Explain what changed your mind.
Useful: It made me realize that… / I came to the conclusion that…
Start with: A small win this week was…
Explain why it was meaningful despite being small.
Useful: It may sound silly, but… / It gave me a boost.
Start with: If I could skip one task, it would be…
Use the second conditional: If I didn't have to…, I would…
Explain what you'd do with that time instead.
Start with: The most useful thing I came across was…
Summarize the main idea and why it's useful.
Useful: The key takeaway is… / I'm planning to apply it to…
Start with: What's been challenging lately is…
Describe the cause and how you're dealing with it.
Useful: I've been struggling with… / I'm trying to…
Start with: This week would be great if…
Use conditionals and wishes: If I managed to… / I wish…
Be specific: one personal and one professional thing.
Start with: A conversation that stuck with me was…
Use reported speech: She pointed out that… / He suggested…
Explain why it stayed in your head.
Start with: A trend I've noticed is…
Give an example and a possible cause.
Useful: It seems that… / This might be due to…
Start with: This month I'm proud of…
Explain the effort behind it.
Useful: It took me… / I managed to… despite…

a1-to-be.forma: I am · you/we/they are · he/she/it is — negativa: am not / isn't / aren't — pergunta: Are you…? Is she…?
a1-to-be.exemplo: I'm 30. She isn't at home. Are you tired?

a1-simple-present.forma: I/you/we/they + verbo · he/she/it + verbo-s — negativa: don't / doesn't + verbo
a1-simple-present.exemplo: I work at home. She works in a bank. He doesn't drink coffee.

a1-sp-perguntas.forma: Do/Does + sujeito + verbo? · Wh- + do/does + sujeito + verbo? — Yes, I do / No, she doesn't
a1-sp-perguntas.exemplo: Do you like tea? Where does she live? — Yes, I do.

a1-there-is.forma: There is + singular · There are + plural — Is there…? Are there…? — There isn't / aren't any…
a1-there-is.exemplo: There is a bank near here. Are there any parks?

a1-possessivos.forma: I→my→me→mine · he→his→him · she→her→her · we→our · they→their — nome + 's
a1-possessivos.exemplo: Her name is Ana. My father's car is old. This book is mine.

a1-preposicoes.forma: AT + horas, at night, at home · ON + dias e datas · IN + meses, anos, cidades, países, in the morning
a1-preposicoes.exemplo: On Monday at 7 p.m. in Rio.

a1-can.forma: sujeito + can / can't + verbo (sem to) — Can + sujeito + verbo?
a1-can.exemplo: I can swim. She can't drive. Can you help me?

a1-frequencia.forma: always · usually · often · sometimes · rarely · never — antes do verbo principal, depois do to be
a1-frequencia.exemplo: I always drink coffee. She is never late.

a1-rotina.forma: wake up · get up · take a shower · have breakfast/lunch/dinner · go to work by bus · do the dishes · go to bed
a1-rotina.exemplo: I wake up at 6, have breakfast and go to work by bus.

a1-was-were.forma: I/he/she/it was · you/we/they were — wasn't / weren't — Was she…? Were you…? — I was born in…
a1-was-were.exemplo: I was at home yesterday. Were you tired?

a2-present-continuous.forma: am / is / are + verbo-ing (agora, temporário, planos combinados)
a2-present-continuous.exemplo: I'm studying now. She's living with her parents for now.

a2-sp-vs-pc.forma: Hábito → simple present (I work every day) · Agora → present continuous (I'm working now) — verbos estativos (like, know, want) não vão para -ing
a2-sp-vs-pc.exemplo: I usually drive, but today I'm taking the bus.

a2-simple-past.forma: Regulares: verbo-ed · Irregulares: went, ate, saw… — negativa/pergunta: didn't / Did + verbo na base
a2-simple-past.exemplo: I went to Bahia. Did you go? I didn't go.

a2-past-continuous.forma: was / were + verbo-ing (cena em andamento) + simple past (interrupção) — when / while
a2-past-continuous.exemplo: I was cooking when the phone rang.

a2-futuro.forma: going to + verbo (plano, evidência) · will + verbo (decisão na hora, promessa, previsão)
a2-futuro.exemplo: I'm going to travel in July. — The phone! I'll get it.

a2-comparativos.forma: curto: -er / the -est · longo: more / the most · good→better→best · bad→worse→worst · as … as
a2-comparativos.exemplo: Rio is hotter than Curitiba. It's the best restaurant in town.

a2-modais.forma: should + verbo (conselho) · must / have to (obrigação) · mustn't (proibido) · don't have to (não precisa)
a2-modais.exemplo: You should rest. I have to work. You don't have to pay.

a2-descricao.forma: adjetivo ANTES do substantivo · What is she like? (personalidade) · What does she look like? (aparência) · She is 30 (não 'has')
a2-descricao.exemplo: She's a tall, friendly woman with short hair.

a2-contaveis.forma: how many / many + contáveis · how much / much + incontáveis · some (afirmativa) · any (negativa e pergunta) · a lot of (os dois)
a2-contaveis.exemplo: How much water? How many people? I don't have any time.

a2-present-perfect-intro.forma: have / has + particípio (experiência, sem tempo definido) — ever, never, already, yet, just
a2-present-perfect-intro.exemplo: I've been to Chile. Have you ever eaten sushi? I haven't finished yet.

b1-pp-vs-past.forma: Present perfect: sem tempo definido / até agora (since, for, ever) · Simple past: tempo definido (yesterday, in 2019, when…)
b1-pp-vs-past.exemplo: I've worked here since 2018. I started in March 2018.

b1-pp-continuous.forma: have / has been + verbo-ing + for (duração) / since (início)
b1-pp-continuous.exemplo: I've been studying English for three years.

b1-past-perfect.forma: had + particípio = ação anterior a outra no passado (by the time, already, before)
b1-past-perfect.exemplo: When I arrived, the movie had already started.

b1-condicionais-0-1.forma: Zero: if + presente, presente · First: if + presente, will + verbo · unless = if not · when/as soon as + presente
b1-condicionais-0-1.exemplo: If it rains, I'll stay home. I won't go unless you go.

b1-used-to.forma: used to + verbo (hábito passado) · be used to + -ing (estar acostumado) · get used to + -ing (acostumar-se)
b1-used-to.exemplo: I used to smoke. I'm used to waking up early.

b1-gerund-infinitive.forma: enjoy / avoid / finish / mind + -ing · want / decide / hope / plan + to · preposição + -ing
b1-gerund-infinitive.exemplo: I enjoy reading. I decided to move. Thanks for coming.

b1-relative-clauses.forma: who (pessoas) · which (coisas) · that (os dois) · where (lugares) · whose (posse) — sem repetir o objeto
b1-relative-clauses.exemplo: The man who called is my boss. The city where I was born.

b1-reported-speech.forma: say (that) / tell someone (that) — volte um tempo: is→was, will→would, did→had done — perguntas sem inversão
b1-reported-speech.exemplo: She said she was tired. He asked where I lived.

b1-modais-deducao.forma: must (certeza) · might / may / could (possibilidade) · can't (impossível) + verbo
b1-modais-deducao.exemplo: He must be tired. She might be at home. That can't be true.

b1-opiniao.forma: I think / In my opinion… · I agree / I don't agree (nunca 'I am agree') · It depends on… · I see your point, but…
b1-opiniao.exemplo: I see your point, but I think it depends on the price.

b2-second-conditional.forma: If + passado, would + verbo (hipótese no presente) · If I were you…
b2-second-conditional.exemplo: If I had more time, I would travel more.

b2-third-mixed.forma: Third: If + had + particípio, would have + particípio · Mixed: If + had + particípio, would + verbo (agora)
b2-third-mixed.exemplo: If I had known, I would have come. If I had slept, I wouldn't be tired now.

b2-passive.forma: be (no tempo certo) + particípio — is made / was built / has been sent / will be done — It is said that… / He is believed to…
b2-passive.exemplo: The bridge was built in 1974. The report will be sent tomorrow.

b2-causative.forma: have / get + objeto + particípio (alguém faz para você) · have someone do · get someone to do
b2-causative.exemplo: I had my hair cut. I got my boss to give me a day off.

b2-modais-passado.forma: must have / might have / can't have + particípio (dedução) · should have (crítica/arrependimento) · could have (possibilidade não realizada)
b2-modais-passado.exemplo: It must have rained. You should have called me.

b2-wish.forma: wish + passado (presente irreal) · wish + had + particípio (arrependimento) · wish + would (irritação)
b2-wish.exemplo: I wish I had more time. I wish I hadn't said that.

b2-contraste.forma: although / even though + frase · despite / in spite of + substantivo ou -ing · However, / Nevertheless, (início de frase) · whereas (comparação)
b2-contraste.exemplo: Although it was late, we stayed. Despite the rain, we went out.

b2-narrative.forma: Past continuous (cenário) + simple past (eventos) + past perfect (o que veio antes) + sequenciadores (suddenly, eventually, in the end)
b2-narrative.exemplo: It was raining and I was walking home when I realized I had lost my keys.

b2-futuro-avancado.forma: will be + -ing (em andamento num momento futuro) · will have + particípio (concluído até um momento) — by, by the time + presente
b2-futuro-avancado.exemplo: This time tomorrow I'll be flying. By Friday I'll have finished.

b2-debate.forma: First of all… · Moreover… · For instance… · On the other hand… · I see your point, but… · To sum up…
b2-debate.exemplo: First of all, it's cheaper. On the other hand, it's riskier. To sum up, I'm in favor.

intermediario: On the one hand… on the other hand…

avancado: It's not as simple as that.

intermediario: I see what you mean, but…
